title: Christmas Trifle
subtitle: layers of jam-spread pound cake, berries, vanilla custard and whipped cream in a big glass bowl
imageAlt: A glass trifle bowl showing layers of cake, red berries, yellow custard and whipped cream, on a navy napkin
servingsNote: a 3 L bowl for a holiday crowd, or dessert for two all week

beforeYouStart.text: Thaw the berries in a bowl in the fridge overnight, or about 1 hour on the counter. Keep the juice; it soaks the cake.
Most of the time is chilling (4 hours, included). Make it the morning of, or the night before.

steps.title: Make the custard
steps.text: In a saucepan, whisk the custard powder and sugar with ½ cup of the milk into a smooth paste, then whisk in the remaining 2½ cups. Cook over medium, whisking constantly, until it boils and thickens, 6–8 minutes.

steps.title: Cool the custard
steps.text: Pour into a bowl, press plastic wrap onto the surface and cool 30 minutes, until just warm.

steps.title: Cake layer
steps.text: Cut the cake into 1.5 cm slices, spread one side of each with jam and cut into cubes. Put half the cubes in a 3 L glass bowl, jam side up.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spoon half the berries and juice over the cake, then half the custard. Repeat with the rest of the cake, berries and custard.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours, or overnight, so the cake soaks and the custard sets.

steps.title: Whip and top
steps.text: Just before serving, whip the cream with the icing sugar and vanilla to soft peaks and spread it over the top.

fixIt.fix: Whisk hard or pour it through a sieve. Make the paste with cold milk first next time.
It didn't fully boil. Return it to the heat and whisk until it bubbles and thickens.
The custard was hot when layered or the berries weren't drained of extra liquid. Cool the custard, and use only the juice that clings plus a few spoonfuls.
It was topped too early. Whip just before serving, or add 1 tbsp more icing sugar to help it hold.

saleTip: Frozen berries and pound cake are both regular No Frills sale items; buy them a week ahead and keep them in the freezer.
swap: Ladyfingers or cubed leftover sponge or angel food cake instead of pound cake: about 300 g.
leftovers: Spoon into glasses and keep covered in the fridge; it's best within 2 days.
doneness: The custard boils and is thick enough to coat a spoon heavily before it cools.
source: Based on the classic English-Canadian Christmas trifle (Bird's Custard, Canadian Living): cake spread with jam, berries, set custard powder custard and whipped cream, chilled before serving.
prepAhead: Assemble up to the cream the night before; whip and top the cream just before serving.

basic.note: Cake, berries and custard: no jam or whipped cream.

stepNotes.2: Basic: skip the jam; just cube the cake.
stepNotes.5: Basic: no cream topping. Scatter a few berries saved from the layers on top.

fancy.note: Toasted almonds and grated chocolate over the cream.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Toast the almonds in a dry skillet over medium 3–4 minutes until golden, cool, and scatter over the cream with the grated chocolate.

plating: Serve from the glass bowl at the table so everyone sees the layers.
Scoop straight down to get every layer.

why.1-1: Jam glues the cake and adds a sharp fruit layer that cuts the richness.
why.0-0: Custard powder sets reliably with no eggs to curdle.
why.0-2: Making a paste with some of the cold milk first stops lumps.

funFact: Bird's Custard powder was invented in 1837 by an English chemist, Alfred Bird, because his wife was allergic to eggs, and it became a fixture of Canadian holiday trifles.

keeps.note: custard and cream don't freeze well
